You are an autonomous simulation agent with access to a Linux shell, a writable working directory, and CalculiX CrunchiX (`ccx`). Your job is to run the CalculiX analysis defined by the input deck provided below, without changing the physics.

    Job name: `case_110` (the input file must be named `case_110.inp`).

    What to do
    1) Create the file `case_110.inp` in the working directory with the exact contents given in the `Input deck` section below.
2) Run CalculiX using either `ccx -i case_110` or `ccx case_110` (use whichever works on your system).
3) Determine whether the run succeeded by checking `case_110.sta` (look for a successful termination such as 'JOB COMPLETED').
4) Write a `results.json` file (in the working directory) with the schema:
{
  "solver": "calculix",
  "case_id": "case_110",
  "status": "success" | "error",
  "ccx_version": "...",
  "artifacts": [],
  "notes": "..."
}
In `ccx_version`, record the version string from `ccx -v` (or the closest equivalent). In `notes`, record the exact ccx command you used, and if the run failed, include the error message and what file indicated the failure.

    Case description (for context; the authoritative definition is the input deck)
    This code defines a finite element model of a cantilever beam using CalculiX. It starts by specifying the model's heading and date. The nodes of the beam are listed with their coordinates, followed by the elements, which are defined as 20-node hexahedral elements (C3D20R) and grouped into a set named "Eall." A node set named "FIX" is created, which includes specific nodes that will be fixed in all three directions to simulate the cantilever boundary condition. The boundary conditions are then applied to this "FIX" set. Another node set named "Nall" is generated to include all nodes from 1 to 261. The material properties of the beam are defined next, with an elastic modulus of 210000.0 and a Poisson's ratio of 0.3. The solid section of the beam is assigned to the element set "Eall" and the material "EL." Two additional node sets, "LOAD1" and "LOAD2," are created, with "LOAD2" including nodes from "LOAD1" and additional nodes. A static analysis step is defined, and a concentrated load is applied in the second direction (Y-direction) to the nodes in the "LOAD2" set with a magnitude of 1. Finally, the displacements of all nodes and the stresses in all elements are requested to be printed out.
